html:
SMTO-AUT-0024 — That account name already belongs to a different Google connection

GUID: c1582aff-4825-5f77-915e-ba25e7711f1e
Slug: google-account-key-conflict
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • The name chosen for this Google connection is already used by a different Google account or a different Google app setup. SMTO left that saved account unchanged rather than replace it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list your connected Google accounts and find the email address saved under the name you used. This tells you whether that name belongs to a different Google account than the one you signed in with.
  2. If you meant to reconnect that same account, ask SMTO to connect again under that name and sign in on Google's page with that same email address. SMTO only updates a saved account when the same Google account signs in again.
  3. If you meant to add a different Google account, ask SMTO to connect it under a new, unused name instead. A separate name keeps both accounts, so the one already saved keeps working.
  4. If the account was first connected through a different Google app entry, ask SMTO to reconnect it through that same entry. Each saved account stays tied to the Google app setup it was first connected with.

What success looks like

  • The Google sign-in page says your email is connected, and each Google account appears under its own name in SMTO's list.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete or rename the existing account entry to free up the name; tasks may still need that account.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The chosen Google account_key already belongs to a record with a different profile type, verified Google subject or OAuth application, so the consent start or save was refused.

What this means

  • The chosen account key already belongs to a different profile type, verified subject or OAuth application. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • The chosen account key already belongs to a different profile type, verified subject or OAuth application.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the key's current account subject and app reference with the intended consent target.

How to fix it

  • Compare the existing record at that account_key (profile_type, subject, oauth_app_ref) with the new consent. Reconnect with the original Google identity through the same google_oauth_app, or choose a different unused account_key; GoogleOAuth.prepare and GoogleProfiles.save_tokens never overwrite a key bound to another subject or app.
  • Use the original Google identity and OAuth application for this account key, or explicitly choose another key.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The saved key retains its original identity, or a separate intentionally chosen key stores the new connection.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
